newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon media workers protest against closures.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon media workers protest against closures.

text.p: Hundreds of Lebanese media workers defied a ban on demonstrations to protest on Thursday against a law slashing the number of private television and radio stations.
Opposition politicians and union leaders led a 15-minute demonstration of 500 media workers after protesters were barred by 150 police from staging a planned sit-in outside the ministry.

Opposition representatives had called on Monday for sit-ins, strikes and street protests "in defense of liberties" after the goverment decided last month to drastically cut the number of private television and radio stations.

Demostrations are banned under a three-year old government decision. Last February Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri called in the army, which imposed a nationwide curfew to prevent street protests called by the labour unions.
But Thursday's protest, led by General Labour Confederation (CGTL) chief Elias abu Rizk and representatives of Christian and leftist Moslem political groups, ended without incident.
The protesters, joined by five opposition members of parliament, chanted slogans denouncing Hariri and his government. "We don't want to see Hariri in power," shouted the crowd.
Some held a wooden coffin with a placard reading "Freedom, democracy". Other signs read: "Lebanon remains with freedom and disappears with repression".

Abu Rizk said a committee, appointed last month by a meeting of 700 trade unionists, MPs, media workers and politicians, would meet on Friday to decide "escalatory steps" to force the government to reverse the law.

Under the law, the government licenced only four private television stations and 11 radio stations, eliminating dozens of television stations and scores of radio stations employing thousands of people.

Three of the four permitted television stations are owned by prominent government figures, including Hariri, while two of the three licenced radio stations allowed to broadcast news are owned by the same people.
